text: SQL Server gives you three backup types, and a real restore strategy depends on knowing exactly what each one captures — full, differential, and transaction log.

A differential backup isn't relative to the last differential — it's always relative to the last full. Log backups aren't snapshots of data, they're a record of every transaction, which lets you restore to an exact point in time.

Full backup captures every page in the database. Differential captures everything changed since the last full. Log backup captures every transaction since the last log backup — and it's the only one that enables point-in-time recovery.

The restore-chain implication trips people up in a real outage: you need the last full, the most recent differential, and every log backup since, in order — skip one link and the chain breaks. Next up: doing this for real, with SSMS and T-SQL.
